title: f83r P1: a loan keeps title while moving custody and preserving a return obligation
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. A whole 72-group paragraph is nominated as a loan account. The same asset may be owned by one party and held by another; permission to use does not cancel the return obligation. Sale and mere work handoff have different joint consequences. All word values and the full narrative are prospective, not an executed reading.

design.whole_content_draft: One asset belongs to B. C may use it under a duty to return it. An actual delivery puts A in C’s custody while B keeps title. The later repeated permissions and return clauses describe the continuing arrangement; they do not perform additional deliveries or erase the obligation. This paragraph need not narrate an actual return. Its final state is B owns A, C holds A, return remains due.
coupled_claims: Permission and a return duty can exist before delivery; mentioning C does not move A.
Delivery changes custody but not title.
A repeated normative clause is not proof that the required act occurred.
design.joint_consequence: After the delivery nominated at f83r.6, title and custody must disagree while the return duty persists. The same repeated title/permission/return words in .7–8 must describe that one arrangement, not reset its actors or silently execute a return.
concrete_rivals: A sale moves both title and custody and normally lacks this same-object return duty.
W41’s work-access transfer tracks who may act, but does not by itself determine title or a future return obligation.
A gift plus later independent advice can mimic isolated phrases but not the single persistent duty if its scope is actually written.
lexical_and_syntax_debts: The owner/borrower/asset roles are guesses. Their names can be jointly permuted without identifying real objects.
Normative versus performed action is an explicit uniform choice for the listed words, not established by context.
Repeated qoteedy qoteedy at .7 is retained as repeated assertion, not counted as two legal acts; syntax for that repetition remains to be explained.
All unknown words could defeat the single-asset history. No hidden transfer/return is supplied to repair it.
The full narrative does not yet align every proposition to a constituent; the proposal needs such an alignment before a fixed test.
